This website includes some of the written sections from the larger paper generated for this project.
For the complete study, along with the two-dimensional visualizations, follow the GitHub link to the Jamaica Bay Water Quality PDF.
This study is completed and published as part of the requirements for a Master of Science in Data Analysis & Visualization at the CUNY Graudate Center.

## Abstract

Jamaica Bay, an urban estuary situated in the southeast of New York City, boasts a long history of
wildlife observation, fishing expeditions, and fertilizer manufacturing. However, its story has been
tainted with issues surrounding water quality damage and public health concerns after large amounts
of artificial alterations in the 1900s, which permanently changed the landscape (U.S. National Park
Service, n.d.). These water quality problems were further exacerbated by unregulated wastewater
treatment and disposal plants in the region, eventually leading to the Jamaica Bay Watershed
Protection Plan of 2005. The plan, implemented in 2007, was designed to reduce
eutrophication-causing nitrogen loads from wastewater disposal (Bureau of Environmental Planning and
Analysis, 2018). The plan has since been updated, and though data regarding water quality shifts has
been collected, it has yet to be analyzed in depth to conclude policy effectiveness. Danielle
Alexander, a former student of Earth and Environmental Sciences at Brooklyn College, conducted an
analysis of the entirety of Jamaica Bay across all stations in 2018. Her work involved PCA as well,
though her methods involved a changepoint analysis of the bay (Alexander, 2018). The purpose of this
project is to build further on her research by conducting PCA on five individual stations across
Jamaica Bay in order to gain granular insights into water quality changes, along with extending the
timeline of the study to include data until 2024.
